sentences.en: I'm afraid of dogs. Every time I see a dog, I get nervous right away.
Today, my friend and I are walking in the park, and see a little dog.
I'm very scared, and stand behind my friend.
Friend says: "Don't be afraid, this dog knows me, it's nice."
I slowly walk over to where the little dog is.
The little dog runs over and sits beside me.

quiz.q: What does the friend say to reassure the narrator?
a: "Don't be afraid, this dog knows me"
"There are no dogs in the park"

quiz.q: What does the little dog do at the end?

grammar.p: 怕 + noun（to be afraid of something）
grammar.e: 怕 followed directly by a noun says you're afraid of that thing.
grammar.x: 我怕狗。— I'm afraid of dogs.

grammar.e: 别 before a verb tells someone not to do something; 别怕 means "don't be afraid."
grammar.x: 别怕，这只小狗认识我。— Don't be afraid, this dog knows me.

grammar.p: 就 + adjective（a quick or direct reaction）
grammar.e: 就 right before an adjective shows something happens right away, as a direct result.
grammar.x: 我看见狗，就很着急。— As soon as I see a dog, I get nervous right away.
